newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher despite steady LME spread.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher despite steady LME spread.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher on hedge-fund buying despite little movement in the London spreads, dealers said.
The LME benchmark cash-to-three-month backwardation was holding firm at $145/$150 at 1445 EDT, up slightly from Friday, but down from $250 a week ago.
Active September delivery settled at 108.55 cents a lb, up 1.15 cents. The spot price ended at 110.90 cents, up 1.10 cents.

"I would have expected people to lose interest in copper as the spreads started to narrow," said one New York commission house broker. "But instead we found a little short-covering providing some support."
"It was the path of least resistance," said one physical merchant of the uptick in prices. "It seemed dead all morning."
On the physical side, merchants reported some buying interest for August deliveries, particularly from the copper rod sectors.
Copper rod is a precursor to wire and cable production and accounts for 60 percent of primary copper demand.
"We've had no trouble moving copper for August," one dealer said. "The wire and cable sectors are pretty busy."
Spot merchant premiums in the Midwest are 2.50 cents over the Comex spot price, off 0.25 cents from last week, dealers said.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1640))
